  PROBLEM: The owner-hold guard reads only the cached linked-PR payloads, so it fails open when they lack `draft`/`title`. The early-phase open-PR guard then fetches a REST payload (`_opr_json`) and never checks it for a hold, so a held, conflicted PR still reaches `_dispatch_review_for_conflicts`.
  WHY: A held PR with merge conflicts still gets a conflict-resolver dispatch, which contradicts the "every phase and every action" invariant. All five reviewers rate this MAJOR; confidence runs 4-5.

  PROBLEM: The ancestor-chain no-op cap arms and the `close_and_reissue` arms (managed and standalone) call `close_linked_pr` and then close the issue without checking `CLOSE_LINKED_PR_HELD_PRS`.
  WHY: When the hold guard fails open, `close_linked_pr` leaves the held PR open but the issue is still closed with `ai:closed`. Sonnet-5_5 listed this only as a hardening suggestion with risk score 1, covering the no-op cap arms. Minimax, gpt-6-luna and glm-5_3-flash rated it MAJOR.
- tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:16373-16377 | severity=nit | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The assertion `"requested_action=skip " not in stdout` can never fail, because the log line ends at the action value. The following `re.search` then checks the output against itself.
  WHY: A regression that selects `skip` for a held `ai:implementing` PR would still pass.
